title: Prince de Conti's mémoire for Laigue, envoy to the Archduke, Paris, 5 March 1649, BnF fr. 3854 no. 43 (ff. 117r-120r)

plaintext.source: Contemporary interlinear decipherment from f. 117r l. 12 onward; the first 12 lines (264 groups) were never glossed

transcription.source: Gallica images, canvases 245-251; glossed groups in n43/pairs_c245-251.txt
transcription.notes: 3,367 code groups in all (264 in the unglossed opening, the rest with their glosses in n43/pairs_c245-251.txt), counted by mk_validation.py 14 Oct 2026; clear words not counted.

system.summary: Numeric letter-and-syllable code: four interleaved single-letter alphabets, five-syllable consonant blocks with a second homophonic series, underline reverses a syllable, nulls 99-250, a few code words.

diacritics.note: An underlined number reverses its syllable (385 ra, 385 underlined ar).

system.notes: Code words 451 la Reyne, 457 cardinal, 458 parlement, 472 l'archiduc, 482 France; the 500s are dates. Split 14 Oct 2026 from conti1649 (nos. 41-42 are Lasry's poly-homophonic letter cipher).

prior_solution.where: contemporary interlinear decipherment on the leaves from f. 117r l. 12; the 12-line opening never deciphered

conditions.human_role: Project-level: obtained a DECODE login with privileges and passed its session cookie (from the browser developer tools) to the model, set up Claude Code with Fable 5.1 or Opus 5, and posed the problem with /goal; occasionally offered encouragement or chose which of the model-identified leads to pursue. No target-specific intervention recorded.

solution.what: Established that no. 43 is a numeric code, a different system from nos. 41-42 (Lasry's letter cipher), so not a crib for them; no printed decipherment of no. 43 found.
Transcribed no. 43 glossed groups with their interlinear readings (about 3,300 pairs) and the 264-group unglossed opening.
Rebuilt the no. 43 key from glosses and layout: interleaved alphabets, syllable blocks of five, underline reverses, nulls 99-250.
Read the unglossed 12-line opening: 220 groups by gloss majority, 24 by structure or nulls, 20 by context.
Scan of ff. 119-120 glosses confirmed 279 de, 364 la, 354 ne; none contradicted.

Split from the former combined target conti1649 (catalogue 26) under the one-key rule (George Lasry, 14 Oct 2026): no. 43's code is unrelated to the letter cipher of nos. 41-42. READING43.md and n43/ moved here; measured with mk_validation.py: 3,300 of 3,367 groups have a value or are nulls (98.0%), the opening 264 of 264.

Statistical validation (docs/_validate.py): 3300 tokens, 218 types, fr-1600-letters order 4: reading -1.882 per letter; random keys -4.1 (z 9.9); key annealed onto shuffled ciphertext best -2.687 (mean -2.701, z 89.4); annealer on the real text -2.496. Verdict: pass.

validation.notes: claimed per-occurrence score -1.904; polyphony 0.026; 67 unread tokens left out; annealer on the real text from random keys reached -2.496

outcome.method: key recovered based on adjacent plaintext
outcome.method_basis: The code was rebuilt from the contemporary interlinear decipherment on its own leaves (about 3,300 glossed groups) and the code's regular layout, then used to decipher the 12-line opening that the clerk left unglossed.
outcome.fraction_read_source: targets/laigue1649/mk_validation.py: code groups of the opening (decode_opening.py values) and the glossed body (pairs files); nulls count as read, groups without a legible gloss as unread

gaps.item: 67 groups without a legible gloss, chiefly f. 117v l. 18, f. 118v ll. 5-8, f. 119v l. 14, f. 120r l. 0
gaps.detail: gloss faint, blotted or struck through

gaps.item: ten context values in the opening (277, 314, 321, 358, 390, 398, 400, 407, 439, 442)
gaps.detail: never glossed elsewhere; fixed by sense alone; none changes a sentence

outcome.notes: Opening (264 groups) new: 220 by gloss majority, 24 by structure or nulls, 20 by context; nine context/structure values later confirmed in the glosses, none contradicted.

credits.note: interlinear decipherment of no. 43, used to rebuild its code and as the text of the body
